Topic: The Geometry of High-Dimensional Spheres: Beyond 3D

Target audience: University students (STEM majors with basic calculus/linear algebra)

Section: section_1 — Introduction: The Dimensional Leap

Lecture lines:
Consider 2D circles and 3D spheres.
Generalize to n dimensions using the Pythagorean theorem.
This leads to the hypersphere definition.
Observe the transition into 4D space.
We visualize the hidden 4D structure.

Planned animations:
Display title: "Introduction: The Dimensional Leap" in #FFFFFF.
Show a 2D square appearing, then morphing into a 3D cube.
Fade in a 4D hypercube wireframe representation slowly.
Highlight the center of the hypercube using a glowing #FFD700 dot.
Transition to the next section with a smooth zoom-in effect.

Section: section_2 — The Counter-Intuitive Volume Paradox

Lecture lines:
Unit spheres shrink as dimensions increase.
The volume tends toward zero.
We use the Gamma function for calculation.
Imagine a unit sphere in a unit cube.
Volume migrates into the corners.

Planned animations:
Show a 2D circle with area #1E90FF, expanding to fill the plane.
Visualize a 3D sphere within a cube, showing corner gaps.
Demonstrate how high-dimensional volume concentrates at the corners.
Color code corner regions with #FF4500 to emphasize density.
Shrink the central sphere to show it becomes negligible.

Section: section_3 — The Concentration of Measure

Lecture lines:
High dimensions exhibit concentration of measure.
Volume collects in a thin surface shell.
The interior effectively becomes empty.

Planned animations:
Represent points as random #FFFFFF dots in a 10D space.
Draw a Gaussian distribution curve in #32CD32 representing distances.
Show points clustering at a specific distance from center.
Display the "concentration of measure" theorem text in #FFFFFF.
Animate points moving towards the shell surface.

Section: section_4 — Real-World Application: High-Dimensional Data

Lecture lines:
High-dimensional data behaves like hyperspheres.
Machine learning maps vectors on spheres.
We use cosine similarity to measure distance.

Planned animations:
Show a dataset matrix with rows labeled features.
Animate feature vectors converging towards a specific manifold.
Highlight outliers in #FF0000 to show sparsity effects.

Section: section_5 — Summary and Conclusion

Lecture lines:
We generalized dimensions through geometry.
Volume paradox reveals counter-intuitive shrinking.
Hyperspheres are concentrated at the surface.

Planned animations:
Summarize key points: Dimension, Volume, Concentration.
Flash each point with a subtle #00FFFF pulse.
Fade out all elements to a clean #000000 screen.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Consider 2D circles and 3D spheres.",
            "Generalize to n dimensions using the Pythagorean theorem.",
            "This leads to the hypersphere definition.",
            "Observe the transition into 4D space.",
            "We visualize the hidden 4D structure."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Dimensional Leap", lecture_lines)
        
        # Color definitions
        colors = [BLUE, GREEN, YELLOW, ORANGE, RED]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]))
        square = Square(side_length=1.5, color=BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(square, 'B2', 'C3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(square))
        cube = Cube(side_length=1.5, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2, color=BLUE)
        self.play(Transform(square, cube))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1]))

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
